sanskrit: अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् । विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम् ॥
hindiTranslation: इसमें कर्मोंकी सिद्धिमें अधिष्ठान तथा कर्ता और अनेक प्रकारके करण एवं विविध प्रकारकी अलगअलग चेष्टाएँ और वैसे ही पाँचवाँ कारण दैव संस्कार है ॥
englishTranslation: The field, the doer, the instruments, the many efforts, and the fifth factor, the unseen force, all shape every action.
essence: Action has many causes, and no one factor owns the result.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Every action depends on several causes: the base, the doer, the tools, the different efforts, and a fifth factor beyond human control.
simpleInsight: It softens blame and pride. Not everything that happens can be reduced to one person’s will.
detailedMeaning: Krishna now breaks action into its causes: the base, the agent, the instruments, the separate efforts, and a fifth factor beyond them. He is showing why no one acts alone.
modernRelevance: A family sits in a hospital corridor after a surgery went wrong, asking whose fault it was. Krishna's list widens the question: the body, the surgeon, the tools, the many efforts, and daiva, the factor nobody controls.
translationLiteral: अधिष्ठानम् (the basis) / तथा (and) / कर्ता (the doer) / करणम् (the instruments) / च (and) / पृथग्विधम् (of many kinds) / विविधाः (varied) / च (and) / पृथक् (separate) / चेष्टाः (efforts) / दैवम् (the unseen force) / च (and) / एव (indeed) / अत्र (here) / पञ्चमम् (the fifth)
insight: Krishna names the five: the seat of action, the doer, the instruments, the various efforts, and daiva.
